source_refs.note: Effect on Ecosystem: a main subheading of 25.4.1 Rapid Growth of Human Populations, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 238-238.

blocks.text: The rapidly growing human population is perhaps the greatest challenge to the future of the biosphere. It is placing severe strains on the global environment. The following are some of these impacts:

blocks.title: For Information
blocks.text: If you weigh all life on Earth, the human population only makes up about 0.01% of the biomass on Earth. About 82% of the Earth’s biomass is made by plants while bacteria make about 13% of the biomass.

items: Habitat destruction and changes in land use
Depletion of natural resources (freshwater, fossil fuels etc.)
Increased waste generation and elevated pollution
Increased chances of new epidemics and pandemics, starvation and malnutrition

blocks.title: For Information
blocks.text: The wealthiest 20% of the world’s population consumes 86% of the world’s resources and produces 53% of the world’s carbon dioxide emissions. Whereas, the poorest 20% of the world consumes only 1.3% resources and emits only 3% of CO₂.
